alignments.note: Connective δέ rendered by the adversative But.
Finite verb; the subject stands on its own pronoun.
Rule 50: the ASV compresses relative plus modal particle into the single word Whosoever, the -soever answering to ἄν, so the pair is one aligned unit headed on that word.
Aorist subjunctive with its licensed English modal; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb say rather than shall.
Rule 20's second arm: no genitive pronoun stands to take the supplied possessive, so the article is what his realizes, with the case preposition to riding along under rule 21.
Bare noun; its determiner and case preposition stand on the article.
As with s007: the supplied possessive is the article's own, no other source word competing for the determiner slot (rules 11, 20).
Rule 77: the relative expanded by a bare supplied antecedent That heads on the relativizer wherewith, which spells the pronoun's own lexeme.

Rule 72: generalizing ἐάν after a relative with no -soever and no other English word answering to it; the generalizing force is absorbed by the English modal, which stays with its verb under rule 9. A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
Inflected verb with supplied subject and auxiliaries; rule 9 heads on the lexical profited.
Rule 36: the English preposition governing the phrase realizes the Greek preposition.

Verbless predicate noun: rules 53, 62 and 68 give the supplied copula and lexical verb to the predicate, which is the only token in the clause to carry them, and the corban formula's dedicatee to God completes what Δῶρον was going to say, so rule 103's licensing test folds it here rather than marking it added; rule 11 keeps the ASV's markup evidence rather than a verdict. Head on the lexical given under rule 17. Marking to God its own added unit under rule 5 remains defensible, God being a full lexical noun and not a word from rule 7's list.

review_notes: s004+s005 joined under rule 50's single-word compression; the -soever is what answers to ἄν.
Both articles take supplied possessives under rule 20's second arm, no genitive pronoun being present to displace them.
The one unrepresented token is the generalizing ἐάν (rule 72).
The materially contested unit is s012: to God folded as a rule 7/103 completion versus marked added under rule 5; the note names both.
